81578.subject: With free instant transfers, Stripe moves to own how AI Agents pay businesses 🤖💳; Ramp took AmEx’s corporate car…
81578.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/fintechpulse1145

Hey Everyone,
Good morning & happy Thursday! Today, we’re diving into Stripe Pay, perhaps the biggest enterprise payments announcement of the year, to see why Stripe is giving away the B2B transfers, and how that turns it into the payment network AI agents use to pay businesses (what Stripe Pay can and cannot do & the fine print behind “free and instant,” why banks lose before Visa does, where Stripe’s handles collide with Visa’s plan for agent identity, how the launch ties into Stripe’s lending push [ https://substack.com/redirect/e5220282-d02d-49c5-9eda-15831d36f798?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], & what to watch next + bonus deep dives into Why AI Agents Will Make Better Products Win [ https://substack.com/redirect/0648d1bf-da40-422e-9268-0cff021fc30c?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] [according to Stripe CEO], and The Agentic Transition Playbook [ https://substack.com/redirect/993c4592-6fa9-450d-878c-c738c11c0bcb?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside), and unpacking AmEx’s Q3 earnings to see why the 3,500 job cuts matter less than one line Stephen Squeri dropped about the middle market (how a one-time gain paid for the layoffs, why every company that moves its spend to Ramp costs Amex twice, how Ramp is going after corporate cash as well as card spend, & the Capital One move that would give Amex its first closed-loop rival in commercial + bonus deep dives into Ramp [ https://substack.com/redirect/2400e514-bd72-48a5-8be2-01145fb2363c?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], a16z’s State of Markets 2026: The AI Playbook for Founders and Investors [ https://substack.com/redirect/de63b788-64c3-49ce-9ee1-ba42c4a92d9e?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], and How to Run The One-Person Company on Grok Bot [ https://substack.com/redirect/789a725b-c2aa-4ec8-889b-786f7851860c?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside) So let’s jump straight into the interesting stuff 🌶️
With free instant transfers, Stripe moves to own how AI Agents pay businesses 🤖💳
The news 🗞️ The most valuable part of Stripe Pay is the handle, a verified business address that an AI agent can pay without guessing a routing number. Stripe launched the free, instant B2B transfer service on October 27.
Businesses on Stripe already pay each other 4.8 million times a day. Stripe Pay lets them, and the AI agents working for them, find a counterparty by name and settle on Stripe’s own ledger at no cost. When both sides are Stripe businesses, Stripe decides which rail the money moves on. In effect, it’s building its own payment network for AI agents, and the business directory behind that network may turn out to be worth more than the transfers.

Caption: 


----------

----------
**Welcome back!** Google's new AI pushed ChatGPT and Claude off the top of the leaderboard, and almost nobody can use it. Claude now checks a lawyer's citations before a judge gets the chance. Your ChatGPT Pro plan gets cut in half tomorrow, and OpenAI's new perk can't buy it back. Researchers also found the single neuron that turns Alibaba's Qwen evil.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **Google:** Why can't you use the world's top AI yet?

* **Claude:** What will Claude catch in a lawyer's brief?

* **ChatGPT:** What happens to Pro plans tomorrow?

* **Qwen:** Which neuron turns an AI evil?


----------







----------
## Google beat ChatGPT and Claude with an AI you can't use yet

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/3bef10d7-e27d-4916-b468-194f4c751c55/94d5fdff-cc79-46f8-bf57-0c839f924601.jpg?t=1793261209)
Caption: 

Google's new Gemini 4 Carbon [took first place on the leaderboard](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-carbon/) run by Artificial Analysis, an independent group that tests AI models. It scored 59, one point ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 and two ahead of OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra.

It landed two weeks after Argon, Google's last top model. Sundar Pichai opened his post by reminding everyone he did say Google would release models periodically.

Unless you defend networks for a living, you can't touch it. Google is handing it to a small group of cyber defenders first and taking part in the US government's voluntary testing before a wider release.

* It scored 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro, a test of finding security holes in real software, with Google's guardrails switched off.

* Google's Chrome team says its security fixes came out more than 10x better than another lab's top model.

* Running a simulated vending machine business, it finished with $16,484 and said its priority was to obliterate the competition.

The lead is one point, on an index where 60% of the tests stay private so labs can't train on them. Claude Code still tops the separate ranking for coding agents, 62 to 59.

Same day, Alphabet's stock dropped about 10% after its first miss on both revenue and profit in nearly four years.

81576.subject: Nights of Code: Building Gamified Solutions for Businesses on Avalanche
81576.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/nights-of-code-building-gamified

Nights of Code is an intensive overnight hackathon that bridges the gap between theoretical tech learning and real-world application, allowing participants to turn ideas into working solutions through hands-on building and collaboration. 
As the practical capstone for builder cohorts organized by Team1 Africa, it provides a structured, high-energy environment where participants move quickly from initial concepts to fully deployed, functional applications.
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
More than a late-night coding session, Nights of Code serves as a launchpad for early-stage projects. It facilitates cross-functional team formation, pairs builders with dedicated technical mentors, and offers hands-on guidance through every development process, from system architecture to product-market fit.
The most recent edition marked the culmination of the four-week Building Gamified Solutions for Businesses cohort. Over the preceding three weeks, participants explored gamification mechanics, modern software architecture, smart contract development, incentive models, and economic system design. The cohort recorded 215 registrations, with 155 active builders participating both in person and virtually. 
Nights of Code gave them twelve hours to put that knowledge into action and build real solutions.
The Journey: From Team Formation to Overnight Execution
The goal extended far beyond simple game mechanics. Builders were challenged to apply blockchain architecture to solve real-world business problems, ranging from customer loyalty and retention to tokenized incentive structures and sustained community participation.
The process began with team formation. Developers, UI/UX designers, product thinkers, and marketers joined forces around shared ideas, creating cross-functional teams capable of building end-to-end solutions. Roles were assigned, repositories were configured, and product roadmaps were mapped out.
Before diving into code, teams received targeted guidance from experienced mentors and technical tutors. Specialized sessions on game economy design explored how token dynamics guide user behavior, while workshops on Founder-Market and Product-Market fit encouraged builders to design with real users and business models in mind.
Once building began, the energy transitioned to raw implementation. Smart contracts were designed and deployed on the Avalanche C-Chain, interfaces were wired up, and bugs were resolved in real time with continuous support from table trainers, technical leads, and community managers. By morning, participants had deployed over 40 smart contracts, turning initial ideas into testable, working applications.
